entries.title: Current identity transactions and pinned OIDC session seam
entries.summary: Add fail-closed current identity/grant transactions and opt-in OIDC code/PKCE browser sessions without mounting shared routes or claiming production provider acceptance.
added: CurrentAuthority reauthentication and same-database all-object/all-operation require/transaction services.
Pinned public-client code/S256-PKCE exchange, one-use attempts, durable hashed opaque sessions and explicit local logout/revocation.
Separate register_identity_routes and isolated mountIdentity UI; offline signed identity/protocol/isolation regressions.
changed: AgencyAccess can consume optional durable sessions while retaining the existing bearer guard map/allowed hook and default-deny unknown routes.
Publish exact same-transaction object/revision/policy integration contract; common app/router/nav/manifests are untouched.
fixed: Stale SQLite WAL snapshots cannot authorize from old grants.
Changed authenticated principals roll back even when both identities hold grants.
Cancellation/expiry after provider exchange prevents session publication and no failed exchange is retried.
verification: 101 focused authorisation/agency/identity/OIDC tests passed with one existing deprecation warning after final stability hardening.
Earlier full suite passed 1420 tests before the final two stability tests; final executed full/native evidence is preserved in the identity lane receipt.
First native run retained as failed: missing setuptools (installed afterward) and frozen Studio shipping-state assertion; eleven other native suites passed. No all-native pass is claimed.
limitations: Not mounted in shared routers/navigation; integrated consuming services must supply exact object ownership/revision/vault-policy adapters and current identity checks.
No live OIDC provider, actual MFA verification, provider account administration/rotation, PostgreSQL row policies, independent security review, live inference or native identity UI acceptance.
Canonical delivery/register/changelog reconciliation and shipping-state test repair are central integration work; no merge/deploy/release/PR change is authorized.

discoveries: Object-only grants and a subset of operations cannot authorize whole-case access or another object; every requested operation must be checked against every consumed object.
An active SQLite read transaction can retain pre-revocation grants; obtaining a writer reservation before authority reads makes that stale snapshot fail closed.
Rechecking only that some current principal has grants can permit a transaction to begin as one actor and end as another equally permitted actor.
A login attempt consumed before provider exchange still needs cancellation and expiry checks before publishing the returned identity session.
Revoking a local opaque session neither terminates a provider account/session nor withdraws independently issued API tokens or future sign-ins.
risks: Fixture identity/MFA claims cannot stand in for independent provider and production-isolation review.
Unused expired attempt retention requires an explicit protected-store host policy, not a hidden background scan.
Frozen shipping-state/native-test mismatch must remain failed evidence until reconciled centrally.
architecture_implications: Keep 8BALL host identity outside the reusable ENDSTATE kernel; reuse existing Identity/Resource/Operation/Grant.
Authentication, current object/matter grants, source-policy/revision review and domain action approval remain separate consuming-transaction checks.
emergence_review.roadmap_decision: Bounded existing_task B03-01 engineering only; EM-139 remains a candidate and production gates stay external. No canonical status or required-scope expansion.
